newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: American Express accuses competitors in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: American Express accuses competitors in Argentina.

text.p: The Argentine unit of American Express has charged Visa International, Mastercard International and local credit card issuer Argencard SA of anti-competitive threats in Argentina.
American Express complained formally to the government's National Commission for the Defense of Competition, Argentina's Economy Ministry said in a statement Monday.

The statement said American Express had accused Visa, Mastercard and Argencard of making "supposed threats" to banks they have agreements with in order to prevent those banks from reaching deals to issue American Express credit cards.

There is clear evidence that there are "oligopolistic" characteristics in the local credit card market, the ministry's statement said. Those include higher fees charged by shops on customers paying with American Express cards.

The commission said it accepted the explanations offered by Visa and Mastercard and that it would take no action now. However, it warned that if these market conditions persist it would take action on its own in the future.

The statement said Industry and Trade Secretary Alieto Guadagni has decided that the "commission will monitor the local credit card market to evaluate if competition improves and charges drop for users" of American Express.
